newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM platinum group metals end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM platinum group metals end sharply lower.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum group metal (PGM) futures ended sharply lower on Thursday with some months tumbling by their daily limits in reaction to Russia's resumption of PGM exports, traders said.
August, October and December palladium futures plunged by their 22 yen per gram limit by the close and benchmark June palladium ended off eight yen at 505 yen.
In platinum, December and April fell by their 50 yen per gram limit and benchmark June closed 35 yen lower at 1,293 yen.
"Selling pressure in PGMs gathered momentum due to Russia's resumption of PGM exports," one trader said.
Russian PGM shipments to Japan under long-term contracts arrived on Thursday, and traders expect supplies to start emerging in the domestic market by next week.

Japanese traders said that the steep fall in spot PGM prices in recent days may be partly due to spot sales by Russia. "Considering the recent sharp fall, it is believed that Russia has been selling supplies in the spot market," a bullion house official said.
Traders said yen-based PGM prices were expected to drift weakly but that physical buying in distant months may prevent prices from falling sharply.
Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended narrowly mixed in directionless trade as the market received little support from the currency market, the traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to four yen higher. Benchmark June was up two yen at 1,143 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $319.60/320.10 per ounce at 0813 GMT, against $318.00/50 in New York on Wednesday.

"Spot gold recovered slightly on short-covering in an attempt to correct the oversold condition, but resistance at $320 would be hard to break through," one trader said. Benchmark June silver was up 1.4 yen per 10 grams at 159.2.
